title: User Confirmation notification templates for the DLP Confirm action: channels, introductory text, languages, link syntax and shared settings

prose.label: Custom messages.
prose.text: {{custom-message-and-languages}} {{message-syntax}} How a rule picks a custom message over a channel's default, and how many custom messages a channel can have, are open {{gap:custom-message-selection}}. The maximum length of the introductory text is open {{gap:intro-text-length}}.

prose.label: Shared settings.
prose.text: {{global-settings}} How the two logo limits relate is open {{gap:logo-limits}}. The on-screen duration for Inline Web DLP confirmations is open {{gap:inline-duration}}.

The Allow, Block and Protect EUNs for Client Connector are in [[zia.eun.client-connector]]; the Confirm action itself is in [[zia.dlp.endpoint-rules]] and [[zia.dlp.rules]]; the auditor email template is a different object in [[zia.dlp.notification-templates]]. Which API object holds the templates is open {{gap:api-object}}.

confirm-action-purpose.statement: If an activity is part of a necessary workflow, Endpoint DLP and Inline Web DLP policy rules can be configured with a Confirm action that requires users to explain the activity and provide justification for why it requires sensitive data.

quotes: If an activity is part of a necessary workflow, you can configure your Endpoint DLP and Inline Web DLP policy rules with a Confirm action that requires users to explain the activity and provide justification for why it requires sensitive data.

default-message-per-channel.statement: When user activity triggers a rule that uses a Confirm action, the service sends the default confirmation message based on the channel assigned to the rule (Network Share, Personal Cloud Storage, Printing, Removable Storage or Inline Web DLP). The default message for each channel gives users a standardized set of justification options that cannot be configured, the language that begins each message can be customized, and the messages can be configured to use the company name and logo.

quotes: When user activity triggers a rule that uses a Confirm action, the Zscaler service sends the default confirmation message based on the channel assigned to the rule (i.e., Network Share, Personal Cloud Storage, Printing, Removable Storage, and Inline Web DLP).

The default message for each channel provides users with a standardized set of options to justify the activity that triggered the rule. Those options cannot be configured, but you can customize the language that begins each user confirmation message.
Additionally, you can configure the messages to use your company name and logo.

other-actions-use-euns.statement: For rules configured with an action other than Confirm (Allow, Block or Protect), the service provides a set of EUN messages that are customized separately.

quotes: For rules that are configured with an action other than Confirm (i.e., Allow, Block, or Protect), the Zscaler service provides a set of EUN messages that are customized separately.

custom-message-and-languages.statement: A custom user confirmation message has a Name and a Channel it applies to, and only its introductory text can be edited. A language can be selected from a drop-down menu to show the introductory text for the message in that language: English (default), Chinese (Traditional), French, German, Japanese or Spanish. If the endpoint OS is set to one of the supported languages the message appears in that language on the endpoint, and in English if the OS language is unsupported; the Preview shows the options in English while they appear in the correct language on endpoints.

quotes: Name: Enter the name for the custom message.
Channel: Select a channel to which the custom message applies from the drop-down menu.
Update the introductory text as needed. Only the introductory text can be edited.
Select a language from the drop-down menu to show the introductory text for the message in that language.
- English (Default) - Chinese (Traditional) - French - German - Japanese - Spanish
The introductory text appears in the selected language; the options remain in English in the Preview but appear in the correct language on endpoints.

If the endpoint OS is set to one of the supported languages, then the confirmation message appears in that language on the endpoint. If the endpoint OS is set to an unsupported language, then the confirmation message appears in English.
evidence.after: - Add a Custom DLP User Confirmation Template

message-syntax.statement: Links can be embedded in the message content with the format __url[Link text | example.com], for example __url[Learn more | https://acme.com/policy], and line breaks can be introduced with the //n character.

quotes: You can embed links in the message content by using the following format: __url[Link text | example.com]. For example, __url[Learn more | https://acme.com/policy].
You can also introduce line breaks in the message content by using the //n character.
evidence.after: - Add a Custom DLP User Confirmation Template

global-settings.statement: The settings page sets the Company Name that appears on each user confirmation message (by default Zscaler), the Company Logo at the top of each message, which must be a PNG file that is 10 KB or smaller (by default the Zscaler logo), and for Endpoint DLP the time messages remain on screen (5, 10 or 30 minutes). The General Details settings are shared with the Client Connector EUN General Details settings.

quotes: Company Name: Add a company name that appears on each user confirmation message. By default, the messages use Zscaler as the company name.

Company Logo: (Optional) Click Upload to upload a company logo that appears at the top of each user confirmation message. The logo must be a PNG file that is 10 KB or smaller. By default, the messages use the Zscaler company logo.
Endpoint DLP: Select the amount of time messages remain on screen (5 minutes, 10 minutes, or 30 minutes).
The General Details settings are shared with Zscaler Client Connector EUN General Details settings.

custom-message-selection.title: How a rule picks a custom message over a channel's default, and how many custom messages a channel can have
custom-message-selection.detail: The pages describe adding a custom message for a channel and the default message sent for a channel, and do not say how a rule selects the custom one or whether a channel can hold more than one.

intro-text-length.title: Maximum length of the introductory text
intro-text-length.detail: Ranges & Limitations gives 500 characters for Notification Message Length for Zscaler Client Connector-Based EUNs; these pages do not say whether that limit applies to the introductory text of a user confirmation message.

logo-limits.title: How the pixel and file-size logo limits relate
logo-limits.detail: The Client Connector EUN settings page says the logo must be a PNG file with a size limit of 20x20 pixels (zia.eun.client-connector:logo-and-duration), and this settings page, whose General Details are shared with it, says 10 KB or smaller. A pixel size and a file size can both hold; the pages do not say whether the same logo is checked against both.

inline-duration.title: On-screen duration of Inline Web DLP confirmations
inline-duration.detail: The settings page lists the duration only for Endpoint DLP (5, 10 or 30 minutes); it lists no duration for Inline Web DLP confirmations. It does not settle gap zia.eun.client-connector:auto-close-values, which is about the Client Connector EUN Auto Close menu.

api-object.title: Which API object holds the user confirmation templates
api-object.detail: No type is registered for the templates, and the OpenAPI /eun path was not checked for confirmation fields.
